passage.title: Reading Part 2 - Test 06
passage.text:
Language learning has undergone a dramatic transformation over the past century. Traditional methods that focused heavily on grammar rules and vocabulary memorization have given way to more communicative approaches that emphasize practical language use. Understanding how these methods have evolved can help learners choose the most effective strategies for their language learning journey.

In the early 20th century, the Grammar-Translation Method dominated language teaching. Students spent most of their time translating texts from the target language to their native language and vice versa, memorizing grammatical rules and vocabulary lists. While this approach helped learners develop reading skills and understand language structure, it did little to prepare them for actual conversations. Students could often write well in the foreign language but struggled to speak it fluently or understand native speakers.

The mid-20th century saw the rise of the Audio-Lingual Method, which was influenced by behaviorist psychology. This method emphasized repetition and pattern drills, with students repeating phrases and sentences until they became automatic. The goal was to create habits through constant practice. Teachers would present dialogues, and students would mimic them repeatedly. However, critics pointed out that this approach produced learners who could repeat learned patterns but had difficulty creating new sentences or adapting to unexpected situations.

Modern language teaching has largely adopted the Communicative Language Teaching (CLT) approach, which prioritizes meaningful interaction in the target language. Instead of focusing solely on grammar rules, CLT encourages learners to use language for real communication purposes from the beginning. Activities include role-plays, discussions, and problem-solving tasks that simulate real-life situations. Technology has also revolutionized language learning, with apps, online platforms, and artificial intelligence providing personalized learning experiences. Today's language learners have access to native speakers through video calls, authentic materials through streaming services, and instant feedback through AI-powered tools. This combination of communicative approaches and technology offers unprecedented opportunities for effective language acquisition.
